note: Base plan: both goods every 3 days at about 1.05× forecast, 9 order days; the main risk is shortages from swings in a single day's demand.
4-day cycle saves fixed fees; the risk is spoilage of good 0 (shelf life is exactly 4 days), higher holding cost and an overflow around day 9.
2-day cycle with little holding or spoilage; the risk is 14 fixed fees (812) and no pooling of demand variance between days.
Lean 3-day cycle at 0.95× forecast, with little waste; the risk is lost margin and penalties (7 per unit of good 1) on high-demand days.
Heavy safety stock (1.2×) against shortages; the risk is write-offs of good 0, holding cost and buying more than sells.
Hybrid: perishable good 0 every 2 days, long-life good 1 every 4 days; the risk is 14 fixed fees and a tight warehouse on the days large batches of good 1 arrive.
3-day cycle with a bit more good 0 (higher margin) and the last order of good 1 moved to day 21 to cover the end; the risk is spoilage of the day-21 batch of good 1 in the last days.
3-day cycle ordering exactly the forecast (1.0×); the risk is a systematic shortfall of about 5% because the demand multiplier averages 1.046.
